title: Dialects and the `use` directive
preamble:
# Dialects and the `use` directive

Dialects, from the language side: what a
dialect is, what the `use` directive does, how it makes a
file a program rather than a library, how a program's
settings resolve at compile time, the built-in dialects,
and what the compile-error contract looks like when a
construct is not permitted. How integrators define their
own dialects lives at [NDLC].

Paired with:

- [LGRA] — `use` is a class-1
  hard keyword; grammar production lives there.
- [LCAP]
  — the capability registry every setting names.
- [LFCA] — the
  capabilities that gate surface constructs, with
  their refactor hints.
- [LLSU] —
  feature inventory, including which features are
  gateable and which are always-on.
- [NDLC]
  — the compiler-CLI integrator path: YAML dialect files
  loaded via `dsc compile -d`.

## What this is not

- Not a dialect-definition spec. How an integrator
  defines a dialect is [NDLC].
- Not the capability registry; see [LCAP].
